title: Elasticsearch
description: Elasticsearch is a distributed search and analytics engine. In .NET applications, it is commonly used with Serilog sinks to store and search large volumes of logs.

data.text: Elasticsearch is a distributed search engine built on Apache Lucene. It stores documents as JSON and provides near-real-time search capabilities. In .NET logging, it is often paired with Serilog to store and analyze large volumes of log events.

data.title: Installation
data.content: Install the Serilog sink for Elasticsearch.

data.title: Sending Logs to Elasticsearch
data.content: Configure Serilog to write structured events to Elasticsearch.

terms.definition: A collection of documents in Elasticsearch, similar to a database table.
A single JSON object stored in an index, representing one log event.
A running instance of Elasticsearch that stores data and participates in the cluster.

data.title: Production Considerations
data.text: Elasticsearch requires careful sizing and monitoring in production. For smaller apps, Seq or Loki may be simpler and more cost-effective.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Elasticsearch stores logs as searchable JSON documents
Index templates and date-stamped indices help manage retention
data.takeaway: Elasticsearch is a powerful choice when you need full-text search and analytics over high-volume logs.

data.title: Exercise: Index Logs in Elasticsearch
data.description: Ship logs to Elasticsearch and query them with Kibana or a simple HTTP request.
steps: Create a console app and add Serilog.Sinks.Elasticsearch
Configure the sink to write to localhost:9200
Log 10-20 events with properties like RequestId, DurationMs, and StatusCode
Query Elasticsearch with GET /myapp-logs-*/_search to retrieve events
data.expectedOutcome: Elasticsearch stores and returns structured log events that you can filter and search.
